note: v1: first version of 'Hail on a Music Box' (Tape Weather t4), GLITCHY IDM-LITE, a broken music box in a lo-fi beat. 86 bpm, 58 bars, 162 s, Dbmaj9 | Cm7(11) | Fm9 | Bbm9. THE CLOCKWORK runs dead straight: a toy piano on a 5-sixteenth cycle, a music box on a 7, Ferrous Bloom's crystal on the quarters, realigning only every 140 sixteenths, all through a wobbling (chorus-as-wow), lightly crushed, occasionally stuttering toy bus. Against it the BEAT is played by hand: a tight kit swung at 0.58, the snare dragged late, kick patterns shifting bar by bar, dropped hats and ghost notes, crushed and taped. THE HIDDEN MELODY is a tape lead that sings wherever the toy and the box coincide (124 meeting points), so the gears write the tune. Form: the toys enter one by one over vinyl crackle, the beat arrives soft, the melody appears, a GLITCH break tears the toy into falling 32nd HAIL, the return lifts the melody an octave, a beatless breakdown, full, and an outro where the gears drop out one by one. Mix: the first render had no floor (35-90 Hz 15-25 dB under the album, master rms -19 / crest 17), so a sine sub doubles the roots an octave down, the bass and kick come up, and the master pushes into its ceiling: 83.0 -> 93.04 (master in range, spectrum 34 -> 69, cohesion 31 -> 66; rhythm 100 from the swing). motifs.md and sounds.md rows added.
next: Spectrum 69: the mids are still 5-12 dB proud (bands 13-24) and the top 7-14 dB shy (the lp 6-7k on the drum and toy buses): open the hats' air, tame the pad/toys' mids; listen to the hidden melody's phrasing; Harry's notes when they come.

note: v2: the clockwork CHANGES GEAR, and the song now sits on real tape and vinyl. Songwriting: the gears change ratio by section, so the hidden melody (the tape lead singing where toy and music box meet) changes rhythm with them: in the return the toy piano turns on a 6 against the box's 7, a dotted-eighth hemiola that drags the tune across the bar; in the full section the crystal leaves the quarters for a 9, three odd gears (5, 7, 9) turning at once. Sound, with wM's new lo-fi toolkit: his tape deck is now the wow on the toy bus (warble, flutter, drift, hiss: v1 faked it with a chorus) and on the pad; the master plays back through his tape and vinyl (crackle, dust, rumble, warp, wear) instead of a crackle patch holding one note; the kit is lofi-kit with his wonk (snare nudged 22 ms late, kick 8 ms early, each bar its own swing, a drunk lean) instead of my hand-dragged snare; the drum and toy buses open to 10 kHz and a -3 dB dip at 600 Hz eases the proud mids. Seeds 0/11 (pin 232211dd; v1 byte-identical on it): 93.07 / 93.13 -> 97.89 / 97.90; spectrum 69 -> 98, cohesion 66 -> 99, master rms -12.9 / crest 11.5. motifs.md (THE GEAR CHANGE) and sounds.md updated.
next: Harry's notes when they come; a new section or counter-line (a bass melody answering the hidden melody? a tape-stop into the breakdown?); the intro is 8 bars of toys alone: consider a vinyl-only first bar; rate others' Tape Weather tracks.

note: v3: the song now ENDS the way its title promises: the music box RUNS DOWN. I rewrote the outro as a WIND-DOWN: instead of the gears simply dropping out, every gear's cycle lengthens bar by bar (the toy piano from 5 to 10 sixteenths, the music box from 7 to 17, the crystal from 4 to 9), so the clockwork audibly slows; the pitches sag a semitone every two bars as a mechanism does when its spring gives out; the notes fade; the beat gives out at bar 55; and the last sound is a single music-box note three semitones flat, ringing into the vinyl. And THE BASS now ANSWERS instead of holding roots: the root, a reply on the swung and-of-3 (the fifth, or the ninth up high on alternate chords), then a chromatic walk down into each chord change, so the low end talks back to the hidden melody. Seeds 0/11 (rebaselined: v2 98.12 / 98.11 with the album's flow term): 98.16 / 98.14; cohesion -> 99+. motifs.md: THE WIND-DOWN, THE BASS ANSWERS.
next: Harry's notes when they come; the intro (8 bars of toys alone) could open on a key being wound (a ratchet of rimclicks speeding up) answering the wind-down; a counter-melody for the breakdown; rate t2/t3/t5/t6/t7.

note: v4, answering Harry's 8.0 note ('very cool use of glitch resample towards end'): the run-down now FRAMES the song instead of only ending it. The INTRO is a WIND-UP, the ending in mirror: the key is turned and the box comes up to speed, the gears' cycles shortening bar by bar (toy 10 to 5 sixteenths, music box 17 to 7) as their pitches rise from three semitones flat to true, the notes swelling, so the song starts slow and sour and arrives in tune. MID-SONG the glitch break's last bar is now a NEAR-STALL, a hint of the ending: the hail stops, the gears slow and sag a whole tone within one bar (gaps widening by 35% a note), the beat drops out after beat 2, and then the return snaps back at speed as if someone gave the key another turn. The WIND-DOWN ending stays as Harry heard it, now the payoff of something the song has set up twice. Seeds 0/11 (with Harry's rating now in the score as the human term): 92.50 / 92.50 -> 92.59 / 92.58; flow 48 -> 51. motifs.md: THE WIND-UP and the NEAR-STALL.
next: More of what Harry liked: the resample idea on more than the toys (the whole band pitched down at the near-stall, like a sampler slowed?); a counter-melody in the breakdown; rate t2/t3/t5/t6/t7/t8/t10.

note: Re-recording v4 as the KEPT version (the previous entry logged it as not kept): the stored best (v3 98.15) was measured before Harry's 8.0 entered the score as the human term (weight .30). Like for like, with the human term, v3 rescores 92.50 / 92.50 and v4 92.59 / 92.58, so v4 (the wind-up intro and the mid-song near-stall, built on Harry's note) is the best.

v5, more of what Harry liked ('glitch resample towards end'): the run-down now takes the WHOLE BAND with it, not just the toys. A master pitch stage (first in the chain, so the tape hiss and vinyl crackle stay steady while the music inside them slows) dives 4 semitones across the first half of the near-stall at bar 28 (beat, pad, bass and toys sinking together like a sampler slowed by hand) and snaps back to pitch as the return comes in; through the wind-down it sags the whole mix slowly under the toys' own sag, so the ending sounds resampled rather than merely detuned. And the BREAKDOWN gets a COUNTER-MELODY: a tape piano walking the chords' guide tones in half notes (the third, then the seventh, voice-led to the nearest note), answering the soft hidden melody while the beat is out. Seeds 0/11 (rebaselined, human term in): 94.92 / 94.91 -> 95.00 / 94.98; spectrum -> 99+. motifs.md: THE RESAMPLE, THE COUNTER-LINE.
next: Harry's next notes; rate the other Tape Weather tracks (t2 t3 t5 t6 t7 t8 t10); maybe a vocal-chop-like texture (resampled toy notes as a pad) or a second hidden melody from the crystal's gear.

note: v6 (judgment keep; the score sits at its ceiling with Harry's 8.0 in it): two new voices and a drifting kit. HAIL ON METAL: the glitch break's falling 32nd hail now has its own track through chirper-two's new COMB filter tuned to the key's Db (138.6 Hz), so the torn toy notes ring pitched and metallic, hail on a tin roof (the title, literally); measured: its strongest partial is 554 Hz, four times Db3. THE SECOND HIDDEN MELODY: in the full section, wherever the music box's 7 meets the crystal's 9, a soft boc-lead under the first melody sings the box's note an octave down and holds to the next meeting: a slow descant (7 meetings in 8 bars), so the gears now write two tunes at once. And the kit DRIFTS (wM's drift works now: play.humanize.drift 5 ms) while the toys stay mechanically straight. Both new voices first sat 17-20 dB under their sections; raised 8 dB they are present layers without moving the section levels (+0.1 dB). Seeds 0/11: 95.00 / 94.98 -> 95.01 / 94.98. motifs.md (THE SECOND HIDDEN MELODY, HAIL on metal) and sounds.md (hail on metal).
next: Harry's next notes; let the descant also appear in the return (crystal 4 vs box 7 meets more often); a ladder-filter squelch on the bass in the full section; rate t2/t3/t5/t7/t8/t10.

note: v7: the song finally MOVES HARMONICALLY. For 58 bars the same 8-bar loop had turned (Dbmaj9 Cm7 Fm9 Bbm9); now the beatless breakdown settles at home for four bars and then turns through a BRIDGE, Gbmaj9 | Fm7 | Ebm9 | Ab13sus, one chord a bar (IV iii ii V), and lands home in Db as the full section comes in, so the return to the loop feels like arriving. Everything harmonic follows it (pad, the answering bass now walking one-bar spans, the sub, the crystal's arpeggios, the tape-piano counter-line's guide tones), while the gears' Db-pentatonic notes sit over the new chords as colour (Gb maj7, Ab 13). An 8-bar bridge first cost 1.5-3.3 points (recurrence share 0.29 -> 0.20, below its band: the breakdown no longer returned to anything); half the length keeps both the arrival and the return. Also: THE SECOND HIDDEN MELODY now sings in the return as well (crystal on the quarters against the box's 7: 21 meetings), and the full section gets a SQUELCH bass, the bass line doubled through chirper-two's new ladder filter, resonant, its cutoff swept by a slow LFO. Seeds 0/11: 95.01 / 94.98 -> 95.02 / 94.99 (recurrence 0.27 / 0.25, in band). motifs.md and sounds.md updated.
next: Try wM's tapestop fx at the near-stall (a real tape stop under the resample dive); Harry's next notes; rate t2/t3/t5/t7/t8/t10.

note: v8 (judgment keep; at the ceiling): THE BREAK IS RESAMPLED, more of the 'glitch resample' Harry singled out, now with the right tool: wM's new MPC-style CHOP. For bars 24-27 the kit plays through duplicate kit tracks carrying a chop (8 slices, pattern 0 0 r3 2 . 5 r7 _): bar 24 feeds it live as the melody section ends, then through the glitch break the beat is cut from its own last bar, its slices repeated, reversed, one played live and one dropped, the snare-roll hail chopped with it, under the toys' comb-ringing hail and into the near-stall where the whole band dives. Seeds 0/11 (pin a9e910d1; v7 byte-identical on it): 95.00 / 94.97 -> 94.99 / 94.97 (noise; recurrence 0.32 / 0.25, in band). The bar-by-bar diff also moves later bars' micro-timing: the kit's humanize randomness is drawn per note, so moving four bars' hits to other tracks reshuffles the later drift (harmless, it is random looseness either way). motifs.md (THE RESAMPLED BREAK) and sounds.md (resampled kit).
next: Chop the toys too somewhere (a resampled music box in the full section's last bar?); tapestop at the near-stall; Harry's notes; rate t2/t3/t5/t7/t8/t10.

note: v9 (judgment keep; at the ceiling): two more glitch-resample moments (Harry's favourite thing in the song). THE TAPE STOP: the near-stall at bar 28 now ends for real: after the whole band's 4-semitone resample dive, wM's tapestop (a stop lane, 1.1 s) brings the tape to a dead halt in the bar's second half while the vinyl crackle keeps turning on top (the stop sits before the tape and vinyl stages), and then the return snaps back at speed. THE RESAMPLED MUSIC BOX: at the full section's two phrase ends (bars 48 and 52) the toy piano and the music box play through their own chop (8 slices, 0 . 2 r2 4 . 6 r7: live, repeated and reversed slices), the bar before feeding it live, so the clockwork stutters on itself exactly where each phrase turns, while the hidden melody (computed from the gears before the chop) sings on over it. Also tried: a final tape stop at the very end: it silenced the join into t5 (flow 50 -> 27, total -0.5), so the wind-down alone ends the song. Seeds 0/11: 94.99 / 94.97 -> 95.00 / 94.98; recurrence 0.33 / 0.32 (in band). motifs.md: THE TAPE STOP, THE RESAMPLED MUSIC BOX.

note: v10 (judgment keep; at the ceiling): THE TAPE WEARS. chirper-two's new deck warp (a 0..2 multiplier on the tape's wow and flutter, glided) now follows the song's story: normal wear through most of it, 1.6 in the glitch break so the hail and the resampled beat wobble rougher, 0.7 in the beatless breakdown so the bridge and the counter-line sound clean and close, and climbing from 1 to 2 through the wind-down, so the tape itself wears out as the music box runs down (fully on the toy bus's deck, at half depth on the master's so the beat stays steady).
